public_rationale: In March 2022, Marcus wrote that scaling laws are observations like Moore's law that may not hold, and that deep learning may be nearing diminishing returns. In November 2024, Andreessen said frontier models were 'hitting the same ceiling on capabilities' with 'a local topping out.' At Ignite, also in November 2024, Nadella said scaling laws 'are not physical laws' but empirical observations like Moore's law, nearly Marcus's own framing. At DealBook on 2024-12-04, Pichai said progress 'is going to get harder' and would need 'deeper breakthroughs.' On the plain reading, these statements are consistent with his prediction of slowing returns from scaling. One limit: none of the leaders endorsed his wider views. Nadella also pointed to a new test-time scaling law, so the agreement is partial. It is about slowing gains from scaling, not about LLMs being a dead end.
limitations: 'Bear out' is a judgment; the outcome depends on reading it as acknowledging slowing scaling gains.
The statements are reported by news outlets, not taken from transcripts.
Marcus's prior prediction comes from his own essay, used only to define what he foresaw.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Recent statements from industry leaders like Andreessen, Nadella and Pichai confirm Marcus's earlier predictions about LLM limitations.

statement.excerpt: The recent statements from Andreesen, Nadella, Pichai, etc. bear out what I foresaw.
statement.document_title: Hard-forked! Casey Newton’s distorted portrait of Gary Marcus and AI skepticism

our_interpretation: Plain reading: in the weeks before the post, Andreessen, Nadella and Pichai publicly said things consistent with Marcus's earlier prediction that scaling up LLMs would hit limits or diminishing returns.

What Marcus foresaw is taken from his March 2022 essay 'Deep Learning Is Hitting a Wall'. It said scaling laws are observations like Moore's law that might not hold, that deep learning may already be near diminishing returns, and that new ideas would be needed. That essay is used only to fix what he predicted, not as evidence that he was right.
'Bear out' is read as: the statements acknowledge slowing gains from scaling. It is not read as: the leaders endorsed all of Marcus's views.
Target period: November 2024 to the post date, matching 'recent'.
criteria.support_condition: Statements by Andreessen, Nadella and Pichai from November to early December 2024 acknowledge a plateau, slowing progress, or doubt about continued scaling gains, in line with Marcus's earlier prediction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The statements actually say scaling continues unabated with no slowdown, or they were misquoted. Or Marcus had not made such a prediction before.

evidence.excerpt: “They’re kind of hitting the same ceiling on capabilities. Now there’s lots of smart people in the industry working to break through those ceilings
evidence.explanation: Andreessen said frontier LLMs were hitting a shared capability ceiling, with 'a local topping out'. That matches a prediction of diminishing returns.

evidence.excerpt: Pichai said “I think the progress is going to get harder,” adding “you’re definitely going to need deeper breakthroughs as we get to the next stage.”
evidence.explanation: Pichai said progress would get harder and would need deeper breakthroughs. That fits Marcus's view that current methods face diminishing returns and need new ideas.

evidence.explanation: Nadella said scaling laws are empirical observations like Moore's law, not physical laws. This nearly repeats Marcus's 2022 wording. The page shows no publication date, so available_at is approximate (Ignite 2024 began 2024-11-19).

evidence.excerpt: He also discussed OpenAI’s new scaling law, which focuses on test-time computing
evidence.explanation: In the same talk, Nadella pointed to a new scaling path (test-time compute). That partly cuts against reading his remarks as conceding that scaling has hit a wall.
